extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational-linguistics researchers and practitioners evaluating LLMs on creative-writing tasks
extracted.subtask_description: Human-evaluation of LLM-generated English creative writing (an open-ended narrative) using multiple subjective dimensions (e.g., fluency, coherence, originality, humor, style); includes methodological note to avoid training-data contamination by choosing a novel scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Included as one of the human-evaluation criteria: 'fluency'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned only in the abstract as a dimension used in human evaluation; no scoring rubric, annotator instructions, or examples are provided on this page (see full paper/PDF for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Included as both a general requirement of creative writing ('requires imagination, coherence, and style') and explicitly as a human-evaluation criterion: 'coherence'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an evaluated dimension in the study; page does not provide operational definition or scoring guidance here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract names originality as an evaluative dimension but provides no further definition or scoring instructions on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract reports results regarding humor (a binary divide in LLM performance) but does not include the evaluation protocol or scales used to judge humor on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Described as a requirement of the task ('requires imagination, coherence, and style') and explicitly listed among evaluation criteria: 'style'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page-level text indicates style was evaluated but gives no further stylistic dimensions, examples, or rubrics here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentioned as a requirement of creative writing in the abstract: the task 'requires imagination'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imagination is presented as a desirable quality of the creative-writing task; the abstract does not state whether it was scored separately or how it was operationalized on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario selection / avoidance of training-data reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological requirement: the authors used 'a difficult, open-ended scenario chosen to avoid training data reuse' (an epic narration of a single combat between a well-known fictional character and a pterodactyl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an experimental-design criterion intended to reduce data contamination: pick scenarios unlikely to appear in model training data. No procedural checklist or automated test is provided on this page; see full paper for implementation details.
